name: The Old Blue Last
summary: A centuries-old East End pub with a live music room and a programme running seven days a week. It has hosted early gigs by acts such as Arctic Monkeys, Amy Winehouse and IDLES, and was owned by Vice from 2004 until the magazine sold its stake in 2021.

music.notes: A place for new bands to cut their teeth, with gigs through the week in an upstairs live room and a free jazz night every Sunday.

accessibility.notes: The live room is on the second floor, and parts of the pub reached by stairs have no wheelchair access. Seating is available; there is no quiet area. Ask the promoter about companion tickets, and contact the venue before visiting with access questions.

cost.notes: Time Out says gigs cost anything from nothing up to £15; the Sunday jazz is free.

evidence.quote: Live music venue, east-end boozer, apparently (definitely) haunted by Shakespeare with a 7-day weekly program

still lives on as a spot for up-and-coming bands to cut their teeth, and is a great place to see some live music on the cheap (gigs range from free to £15). It also hosts free weekly jazz nights on Sundays.
Located on the second floor, our 150-capacity live room has seen a whole host of events, from live bands, karaoke, private parties, club nights, and more.
Some areas of the venue are accessed by stairs and, unfortunately, there is no wheelchair access to these areas.

Quiet areas: Please note that we do not have a dedicated quiet or safe area.
If you require a companion ticket, please contact the event promoter directly before the event.
